title: Fppf descent and base change of four algebraic-space morphism properties
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], and let $h:X\to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Fibre products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. An fppf covering $\{Y_i\to Y\}_{i\in I}$ is a set-indexed jointly surjective family of flat locally finitely presented maps, with flatness and local finite presentation tested on etale scheme charts [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. For algebraic spaces, affine means that every affine scheme base change has affine scheme source [pqf-def-affine-morphism]; finite type means quasi-compact and locally of finite type on etale scheme charts [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], where quasi-compact means that pullback to any quasi-compact scheme has quasi-compact source and an algebraic space is quasi-compact if it admits a quasi-compact surjective etale scheme atlas [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]; quasi-finite means finite type with finite geometric fibres, namely fibres over spectra of algebraically closed fields [def-weil-algebraic-closure]; separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion on every scheme base change [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Each property $P$ in the list affine, finite type, quasi-finite, separated is invariant under isomorphisms of morphisms and preserved by arbitrary algebraic-space base change. Separately for each $P$ and every fppf covering as above,
$$P(h)\ \Longleftrightarrow\ \text{for every }i\in I,\ P(X\times_Y Y_i\to Y_i).$$

Base change: spaces-morphisms.tex Tags 03WI (lemma-base-change-affine), 03XH (lemma-base-change-finite-type), 03XL (lemma-base-change-quasi-finite), 03KL (lemma-base-change-separated).

proof.text: For $h:X\to Y$, its quasi-compactness convention is unchanged if quasi-compact algebraic-space tests are allowed: choose a quasi-compact surjective etale scheme atlas $U\to Z$ of such a test $Z$. Scheme-test quasi-compactness supplies a quasi-compact scheme atlas $V\to X\times_YU$. Its composite $V\to X\times_YZ$ is surjective etale by base change and composition [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests], so the latter space is quasi-compact. The converse just restricts the tests to schemes; [lem-sfb-space-quasicompact-affine-tests] also permits affine tests. Now prove the arbitrary base-change assertions. For affineness of the pullback $h'$ along $Y'\to Y$, every affine scheme test $T\to Y'$ has source $(X\times_YY')\times_{Y'}T\cong X\times_YT$, which is affine by affineness of $h$. The isomorphism forgets the redundant $Y'$ coordinate, with inverse inserting its fixed map from $T$. Finite type is preserved by [lem-sfb-stack-finite-type-calculus], using its explicit agreement with ordinary algebraic-space notions. Separatedness is preserved by [lem-sfb-space-separated-fp-composition]. Suppose $h$ is quasi-finite in the precise finite-geometric-fibre sense of the statement. Its pullback $h':X\times_YY'\to Y'$ is of finite type by the preceding assertion. For every algebraically closed field $\Omega$ and $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y'$, its fibre identifies with $X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. On any test scheme the identification forgets the redundant $Y'$ coordinate and its inverse inserts the prescribed map to $Y'$. Thus its point set is finite by the hypothesis on $h$. This proves base-change stability for that definition of quasi-finite and hence every forward covering implication.

source.place: Tags 041Z, 041U, 0421, 0427: forward implications; spaces-morphisms.tex 03WI, 03XH, 03KL; finite-geometric-fibre convention handled directly

proof.text: For reverse implications fix an affine scheme $T\to Y$. Apply [lem-sfb-space-fppf-finite-affine-refinement] to obtain $p:T'=\coprod_{j\in J}V_j\to T$, flat surjective between affines, with $\{p\}$ both fppf and fpqc, and maps $V_j\to Y_{a(j)}$ over $Y$. Write $E=X\times_YT$ and $E'=E\times_TT'$. The restriction $E_j=E'\times_{T'}V_j$ identifies with $X\times_YV_j$ and hence with $(X\times_YY_{a(j)})\times_{Y_{a(j)}}V_j$. These identifications match the projections because all descriptions give the same pair of sections, one in $X$ and one in $V_j$, with equal image in $Y$. By Step 1, each $E_j\to V_j$ has whichever one of the four properties is assumed for all the original pullbacks. This refinement will be used for affineness and for scheme tests of the diagonal.

source.place: Tag 041Z, affine-test reduction, and spaces-topologies.tex 0DFQ, finite affine refinement

proof.text: Assume all the original pullbacks are affine. Then each $E_j$ of Step 2 is an affine scheme since $V_j$ is affine. We check that $E'$ is represented by $\coprod_jE_j$. A section of $E'$ on a scheme $W$ includes a map $W\to T'$. The inverse images $W_j$ of the disjoint open-and-closed summands $V_j$ partition $W$; on $W_j$ the section is exactly a map to $E_j$. Conversely these local sections glue uniquely since $E'$ is a sheaf, giving a section of $E'$. The coproduct partition description in [lem-trf-fppf-sheaf-coproduct-partition] gives exactly the same data for the coproduct of the representing sheaves; the scheme coproduct represents it, because maps to a disjoint union are maps on such a clopen partition [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. These constructions are inverse and commute with restriction, also for $J=\varnothing$. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-finite-affine-coproduct-spectrum] makes this finite coproduct of affine schemes affine.

source.place: Tag 041Z, affine refinement assembly; finite disjoint union identification expanded on sections

proof.text: An affine scheme is quasi-affine by taking its whole open subscheme, which is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Thus $E'$ is a quasi-affine scheme. Apply [lem-sfb-space-quasi-affine-affine-descent] to $E\to T$ and the flat surjection of affine schemes $p:T'\to T$ from Step 2. It says that $E$ is represented by a quasi-affine scheme, in particular by a scheme; it does not yet assert affineness. Now $E\to T$ is a scheme morphism and its pullback to the fpqc covering $\{p\}$ is affine, by [pqf-lem-affine-local-target] applied to the singleton affine open cover of $T'$ by itself, whose inverse image is the affine scheme $E'$. [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-descend-affine] says that $E\to T$ is affine. Since $T$ is affine, $E$ itself is affine by the defining inverse-image criterion [pqf-def-affine-morphism]. This holds for every affine $T\to Y$, which is exactly affineness of $h$ in the statement.

source.place: Tag 041Z, scheme representability followed by scheme affineness descent; representability supplied here by the stronger quasi-affine input 0423

proof.text: Assume all the original pullbacks are of finite type. Their local finite type descends along the given fppf family by [lem-sfb-space-lft-smooth-fpqc-locality], and their quasi-compactness descends by [lem-sfb-space-quasicompact-fppf-local]. The latter uses tests on all quasi-compact algebraic spaces; Step 1 proves this equivalent to tests on quasi-compact schemes, and [lem-sfb-space-quasicompact-affine-tests] further permits affine tests. Consequently $h$ is locally of finite type and quasi-compact, which is finite type. Each property was descended separately; no flatness or separation of $h$ was assumed.

Assume all the original pullbacks $h_i$ are separated, and put $D=X\times_YX$. The relative diagonal $\Delta_h:X\to D$ is representable: for any scheme $T\to D$, its source on that test is the pullback of the representable absolute diagonal of $X$ along the pair of maps $T\rightrightarrows X$. Explicitly, the section consists of $x\in X(W)$ and $t\in T(W)$ for which both $X$ coordinates of $t$ equal $x$; the equality in $Y$ is then automatic. This is a scheme by [def-trf-algebraic-space]. It suffices to prove it a closed immersion over each affine open $T_0\subseteq T$, since [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-affine-cover-criterion] first supplies affine inverse images and surjective ring maps on those opens, and then its converse supplies the global closed immersion. Apply the refinement in Step 2 to the composite $T_0\to D\to Y$, giving $T'=\coprod_jV_j\to T_0$.

source.place: Tag 0421 (lemma-descending-property-separated), diagonal argument, with affine scheme tests explicit

proof.text: The scheme test of $\Delta_h$ over each $V_j$ in Step 6 is a scheme test of $\Delta_{h_{a(j)}}$: its two $X$ coordinates together with the chosen $Y_{a(j)}$ coordinate give a map $V_j\to X_{a(j)}\times_{Y_{a(j)}}X_{a(j)}$. Pulling back the latter diagonal imposes precisely that the two $X$ coordinates agree. Hence it is a closed immersion. The maps $V_j\to T_0$ are an fppf scheme covering by the refinement lemma and hence an fpqc covering by [lem-trf-fppf-covering-is-fpqc]. Apply [lem-pc-fpqc-descend-closed-immersion] to the represented scheme morphism over $T_0$. It is a closed immersion. Step 6 gives that every scheme test of $\Delta_h$ is a closed immersion, so $h$ is separated. This never requires $X$ or $D$ to be schemes.

source.place: Tag 0421, final descent of the diagonal; scheme descent 02L6

proof.text: Assume all $h_i$ are quasi-finite as defined in the statement. Step 5 gives finite type for $h$. Fix an algebraically closed field $\Omega$ and $y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$. By [def-trf-algebraic-space-jointly-surjective-family], there are $i$, a field extension $L/\Omega$, and a lift $\operatorname{Spec}L\to Y_i$. Choose an algebraic closure $\Lambda$ of $L$ using [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Then $F_\Lambda=X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\Lambda$ is a geometric fibre of $h_i$, so its point set is finite. Put $F_\Omega=X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. The projection $|F_\Lambda|\to|F_\Omega|$ is surjective: represent any point of $F_\Omega$ by $\operatorname{Spec}K\to F_\Omega$, so $K/\Omega$ is a field extension. Apply [lem-trf-family-common-extension-field] to $K/\Omega$ and $\Lambda/\Omega$, obtaining a common extension $M$ with embeddings agreeing on $\Omega$. The representative over $M$ and the map $\operatorname{Spec}M\to\operatorname{Spec}\Lambda$ give a point of $F_\Lambda$ above the original class by the fibre-product universal property. A surjective image of a finite set is finite. Thus every geometric fibre of $h$ is finite, giving quasi-finiteness. No claim that finite topological fibres are discrete for arbitrary spaces is used.

source.place: Tag 0427, fppf specialization; finite-geometric-fibre formulation handled directly by field lifting and amalgamation

proof.text: Finally let $(u,v)$ be an isomorphism from $h:X\to Y$ to $\widetilde h:\widetilde X\to\widetilde Y$. Every scheme test of either arrow, after composing its target map with $v$ or $v^{-1}$, is isomorphic to the corresponding test of the other; the inverse maps are induced by $u$ and $u^{-1}$. Hence affineness and finite geometric fibre sets are invariant (the latter sets are bijective). Quasi-compactness is invariant because an isomorphism carries a quasi-compact etale atlas to one, and the same test correspondence applies. A compatible etale scheme chart pair for $h$ is one for $\widetilde h$ after composing the chart maps with $u,v$, with the same scheme map between the charts; therefore local finite type, and with quasi-compactness finite type, are invariant. The two relative diagonals have isomorphic scheme tests by the same pair-of-sections description, so separatedness is invariant. These observations also cover the empty spaces. In particular the empty covering can occur only over the empty $Y$, whence $X$ is empty; the empty affine scheme, vacuous chart tests, empty fibres and empty diagonal satisfy all four properties. Together with Steps 1, 4, 5, 7 and 8 this proves each asserted equivalence and all the stated invariances.
